extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and researchers considering submitting a manuscript to Forum of Mathematics, Pi
extracted.subtask_description: Information page for authors about the Forum of Mathematics, Pi journal: its aims, scope, editorial standards, and practical submission notes (links to author instructions and the partner submission system).

rubrics_metrics.name: Papers published are of the highest quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Forum of Mathematics, Pi publishes papers 'of the highest quality.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page emphasizes that published papers should be of the highest quality and of real interest to a broad cross-section of all mathematicians. This is presented as the primary qualitative standard for acceptance; no numerical scoring or detailed acceptance criteria are given on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: strong research from pure mathematics and related areas
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Strong research papers from all parts of pure mathematics and related areas are welcomed.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal is generalist within mathematics and invites submissions across pure mathematics and related areas; papers should be of broad interest to mathematicians. The statement defines topical scope rather than technical acceptance thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-review standards set by an international editorial board
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer-review standards are set by an international editorial board 'of the highest calibre.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance is subject to peer review overseen by the editorial board; the page signals rigorous, internationally benchmarked review but does not enumerate specific review criteria (e.g., novelty, correctness) on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access publication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Forum of Mathematics, Pi offers fully open access publication with all published papers free online in perpetuity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page states the journal is an open access alternative to leading generalist mathematics journals and that published papers remain free online forever. Authors should be aware of the journal’s OA status and any related policies (fees, licenses) which are not detailed here but likely on the author instructions pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the partner submission system; account required
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts must be submitted via a partner secure submission system, and authors will need an account separate from their Cambridge Core account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page instructs prospective authors to proceed to the partner submission system and notes that login/submission support is available via submission and support pages. This is a procedural requirement prior to submission rather than an acceptance-quality criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors should review author instructions / preparing your materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are asked to 'please review this journal's author instructions, particularly the preparing your materials page, before submitting your manuscript.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly directs authors to read the author instructions (and a specific 'preparing your materials' page) before submission; those linked pages presumably contain formatting, ethical, and material-preparation requirements not repeated on this overview page.
